title: Subject Pronouns

items.prompt: Which pronoun means “she”?
items.feedback: ✔️ هِيَ means “she”. هُوَ means “he”.

items.prompt: You are speaking to one female student. Choose “you”.
items.feedback: ✔️ One female addressee = أَنْتِ . The kasra sound at the end helps distinguish it from أَنْتَ .

items.prompt: Which form addresses two people of any gender?
items.feedback: ✔️ أَنْتُمَا = you two. It works for two males, two females or a mixed pair.

items.prompt: Which pronoun refers to an all-female group?
items.feedback: ✔️ هُنَّ refers to three or more females. A mixed group normally uses هُمْ .

items.prompt: Complete: هِيَ ________ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ.
items.feedback: ✔️ “She studies” = هِيَ تَدْرُسُ . The verb begins with تـ .

items.prompt: In a simple present description, which is correct?
items.feedback: ✔️ Arabic normally uses no separate present-tense word for “am/is/are” in a simple nominal sentence: أَنَا طَالِبَةٌ .

items.prompt: First person + plural
items.feedback: ✔️ The speakers include themselves: نَحْنُ = we.

items.prompt: Second person + singular + masculine
items.feedback: ✔️ You are speaking directly to one male: أَنْتَ .

items.prompt: Third person + singular + feminine
items.feedback: ✔️ One female spoken about = هِيَ .

items.prompt: Why are أَنَا and نَحْنُ not labelled masculine or feminine?
options: First-person pronouns are shared by all genders
items.feedback: ✔️ A male or female speaker says أَنَا ; any group says نَحْنُ .

items.prompt: How many distinct written independent subject pronouns are there?
items.feedback: ✔️ There are 12 distinct written forms arranged across 14 grammatical slots.

items.prompt: She is a teacher.
items.feedback: ✔️ Both pronoun and profession are feminine: هِيَ مُعَلِّمَةٌ .

items.prompt: You two are friends (two females).
items.feedback: ✔️ You are addressing exactly two people: أَنْتُمَا . Feminine dual predicate: صَدِيقَتَانِ .

items.prompt: They are in the library (all-female group).
items.feedback: ✔️ An all-female group spoken about = هُنَّ .

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly means “I am a student” for a female speaker?
items.feedback: ✔️ أَنَا is shared by male and female speakers; the predicate shows the speaker’s gender.

items.prompt: Ali, Sara and Mona are students. Which pronoun refers to the mixed group?
items.feedback: ✔️ Three people form a plural group, and a mixed group normally uses هُمْ .
✔️ One female addressed: أَنْتِ تَكْتُبِينَ .
✔️ Masculine/mixed plural third person: هُمْ يَذْهَبُونَ .

items.prompt: Two sisters are studying. Complete: هُمَا ________.
items.feedback: ✔️ Two females: هُمَا تَدْرُسَانِ .

items.prompt: Which sentence is accurate?
items.feedback: ✔️ “She goes” = هِيَ تَذْهَبُ .

items.prompt: Which sentence means “You all write” to an all-female group?
items.feedback: ✔️ Addressed female plural: أَنْتُنَّ تَكْتُبْنَ .

items.prompt: Why can أَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ stand without أَنَا ?
items.feedback: ✔️ The subject is built into the verb form. The explicit pronoun remains useful for contrast, emphasis or clarity.

items.prompt: Who does the first هُوَ refer to?
items.feedback: ✔️ The text says هُوَ أَبِي — he is my father.

items.prompt: هُمَا طَالِبَانِ refers to:
items.feedback: ✔️ Masculine dual طَالِبَانِ follows أَخَوَانِ .

items.prompt: Why is the later verb تَقْرَآنِ rather than يَقْرَآنِ ?
options: All dual verbs begin with ت
items.feedback: ✔️ The subject is the two sisters, so feminine dual uses تَـ...ـَانِ .

items.prompt: Who is included in نَحْنُ نَذْهَبُ ?
items.feedback: ✔️ نَحْنُ includes the speaker, Layla, and the family group in context.

items.prompt: Which pronoun occurs with both masculine and feminine dual descriptions?
items.feedback: ✔️ هُمَا is shared by both genders; the following words show the distinction.

items.prompt: Who says أَنَا ?
items.feedback: ✔️ The speaker introduces himself: أَنَا يُوسُفُ .

items.feedback: ✔️ هٰذَا صَدِيقِي عُمَرُ، وَهُوَ...

items.feedback: ✔️ Maryam is Yusuf’s sister and studies Arabic.

items.prompt: The three new students are referred to as:
items.feedback: ✔️ A plural student group described with the masculine/mixed form uses هُمْ .

items.prompt: What shows that the final هُمَا refers to two females?
items.feedback: ✔️ The feminine dual adjective and the verb beginning with تـ reveal the referents’ gender.

items.feedback: ✔️ Second-person dual: أَنْتُمَا .

items.prompt: An all-female group says “we”. Which pronoun?
items.feedback: ✔️ First-person plural has no gender distinction: نَحْنُ .

items.prompt: Choose: “They two are doctors” for two women.
items.feedback: ✔️ Pronoun هُمَا ; feminine dual predicate طَبِيبَتَانِ .

items.prompt: Complete: أَنْتُمْ ________ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ.
items.feedback: ✔️ Addressed masculine/mixed plural: أَنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ .

items.prompt: Two girls write. Choose the full sentence.
items.feedback: ✔️ Feminine dual third person: هُمَا تَكْتُبَانِ .

items.feedback: ✔️ No separate present copula is required.

items.prompt: Which pronoun normally refers to Ali, Sara and Fatima together?
items.feedback: ✔️ A mixed plural human group normally takes هُمْ .

blocks: ## Pronouns tell us who is speaking and who is being described

English often hides gender and number inside one word such as you . Arabic makes those distinctions visible. A correct pronoun helps you understand a text, follow a listening passage, choose the right verb form and write with precision.
### 👂 Track speakers
In listening and reading, pronouns help you work out whether the speaker means one person, two people or a whole group.
### 🧩 Control agreement
The pronoun controls verb prefixes and endings, and it affects nouns and adjectives used to describe the subject.
### 💬 Communicate naturally
Use أَنَا، نَحْنُ، هُوَ، هِيَ، هُمْ and the other forms to introduce, compare, explain and refer back to people.
[callout] The big English–Arabic difference English has one general word “you”. Arabic has five: أَنْتَ، أَنْتِ، أَنْتُمَا، أَنْتُمْ، أَنْتُنَّ . You must decide gender and number before choosing.
## Use the chapter at the depth you need
You do not have to complete every section at once. Revise the Core route first, then deepen or stretch when you are ready.
### Recognise and choose
- Identify the 12 written forms.
- Choose by person, gender and number.
- Build simple present descriptions.
### Apply and agree
- Use pronouns with present-tense verbs.
- Track references in short texts.
- Use dual and plural forms accurately.
### Explain and refine
- Know when an explicit pronoun may be omitted.
- Handle feminine dual verb agreement.
- Recognise non-human plural agreement.
## What do you already know?
Answer without looking ahead. The explanations will tell you what to revisit.
## Every pronoun answers three questions
Do not memorise the list as twelve unrelated words. Build each form from person + number + gender .
### 1️⃣ Person
First person: the speaker — I / we. Second person: the person addressed — you. Third person: someone spoken about — he / she / they.
### 2️⃣ Number
Singular: one. Dual: exactly two. Plural: three or more.
### 3️⃣ Gender
Arabic distinguishes masculine and feminine in many second- and third-person forms. First-person pronouns do not change for gender.

[callout] 14 slots but 12 written forms Traditional grammar often displays fourteen person–gender–number slots. Two forms are written twice because they serve both masculine and feminine dual: أَنْتُمَا and هُمَا . Therefore, you learn 12 distinct written forms .

## Singular, dual and plural forms
Learn the full system as a grid. The dual forms are especially important because English usually uses the same word for one person, two people and a group.

TABLE: Person | Number / gender | Arabic | Meaning | Useful note // 1st | singular | أَنَا | I | No gender distinction // 1st | plural | نَحْنُ | we | No gender distinction; includes the speaker // 2nd | singular masculine | أَنْتَ | you | Addressing one male // 2nd | singular feminine | أَنْتِ | you | Addressing one female // 2nd | dual, both genders | أَنْتُمَا | you two | Two males, two females or a mixed pair // 2nd | masculine / mixed plural | أَنْتُمْ | you all | All-male or mixed group // 2nd | feminine plural | أَنْتُنَّ | you all | All-female group // 3rd | singular masculine | هُوَ | he | One male spoken about // 3rd | singular feminine | هِيَ | she | One female spoken about // 3rd | dual, both genders | هُمَا | they two | The following verb/adjective may reveal gender // 3rd | masculine / mixed plural | هُمْ | they | All-male or mixed group // 3rd | feminine plural | هُنَّ | they | All-female group
### 👥 Mixed groups
When a group contains males and females, standard Arabic normally uses the masculine plural form:
[example] عَلِيٌّ وَمَرْيَمُ وَسَلْمَىٰ؟ هُمْ طُلَّابٌ. Ali, Maryam and Salma? They are students.
### 2️⃣ The dual
هُمَا and أَنْتُمَا do not themselves show gender. Later agreement may show it:
[example] هُمَا مُجْتَهِدَانِ. They two are hardworking (masculine/mixed).
[example] هُمَا مُجْتَهِدَتَانِ. They two are hardworking (feminine).
## Arabic normally needs no separate “am, is or are” in a simple present description
A pronoun can be the topic of a present-time nominal sentence. Put the information directly after it.
[ar] هِيَ
[ar] طَالِبَةٌ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ
### Pronoun + noun
[example] هُوَ مُهَنْدِسٌ. He is an engineer.
[example] هُنَّ طَالِبَاتٌ. They are students (all female).
### Pronoun + adjective
[example] أَنْتَ مُجْتَهِدٌ. You are hardworking (one male).
[example] أَنْتِ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ. You are hardworking (one female).
### Pronoun + place phrase
[example] نَحْنُ فِي الْفَصْلِ. We are in the classroom.
[example] هُمْ مِنْ لَنْدَنَ. They are from London.

[callout] Accurate, not absolute This rule applies to a simple present-time nominal sentence . Arabic can express “was” with كَانَ and present negation with لَيْسَ , but those belong to later grammar study. Do not translate English “am/is/are” word for word here.

## The pronoun controls the present-tense verb form
The beginning and ending of the verb reveal person, number and often gender. This is why the subject pronoun may sometimes be left unstated when the verb already makes the subject clear.

[callout] Important usage note أَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ. already means “I study Arabic.” Adding أَنَا is correct when you want clarity, contrast or emphasis: أَنَا أَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ، وَهُوَ يَدْرُسُ الْفَرَنْسِيَّةَ.

TABLE: Pronoun | Meaning | Verb form: دَرَسَ / يَدْرُسُ | Pattern to notice // أَنَا | I | أَدْرُسُ | أَـ // نَحْنُ | we | نَدْرُسُ | نَـ // أَنْتَ | you m. sg. | تَدْرُسُ | تَـ // أَنْتِ | you f. sg. | تَدْرُسِينَ | تَـ...ـِينَ // أَنْتُمَا | you two | تَدْرُسَانِ | تَـ...ـَانِ // أَنْتُمْ | you m./mixed pl. | تَدْرُسُونَ | تَـ...ـُونَ // أَنْتُنَّ | you f. pl. | تَدْرُسْنَ | تَـ...ـْنَ // هُوَ | he | يَدْرُسُ | يَـ // هِيَ | she | تَدْرُسُ | تَـ // هُمَا | they two, m./mixed | يَدْرُسَانِ | يَـ...ـَانِ // هُمَا | they two, f. | تَدْرُسَانِ | تَـ...ـَانِ // هُمْ | they m./mixed pl. | يَدْرُسُونَ | يَـ...ـُونَ // هُنَّ | they f. pl. | يَدْرُسْنَ | يَـ...ـْنَ
### Same-looking verb forms
أَنْتَ تَدْرُسُ and هِيَ تَدْرُسُ share the same verb form. Context or the explicit pronoun tells you whether it means “you study” or “she studies”.
### The feminine dual detail
The pronoun stays هُمَا , but two females take تَدْرُسَانِ ; two males or a mixed pair take يَدْرُسَانِ .

## Use pronouns to understand and communicate
Grammar becomes memorable when it carries meaning. Work through the reading, listening, speaking and writing tasks at your own pace.
### Reading workshop Who does each pronoun refer to?

[example] أَنَا لَيْلَىٰ، وَأَنَا طَالِبَةٌ فِي مَدْرَسَةٍ فِي لَنْدَنَ. أَعِيشُ مَعَ أُسْرَتِي. هُوَ أَبِي، وَهُوَ مُهَنْدِسٌ. هِيَ أُمِّي، وَهِيَ مُعَلِّمَةٌ. لِي أَخَوَانِ. هُمَا طَالِبَانِ، وَهُمَا يُحِبَّانِ الرِّيَاضَةَ. لِي أُخْتَانِ أَيْضًا. هُمَا مُجْتَهِدَتَانِ، وَهُمَا تَقْرَآنِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. فِي نِهَايَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ نَحْنُ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَةِ.
Later-stage reading may contain fewer vowel marks in an examination. This supported version keeps the target grammar visible.
### Listening studio Track the people
Listen twice without looking. Then answer the questions and use the script to check and repair your answers.
### Speaking studio Introduce your circle
Prepare a short spoken introduction about yourself and people around you. Use at least six different pronouns.
[callout] Required Arabic evidence أَنَا... / نَحْنُ... / هُوَ... / هِيَ... / هُمَا... / هُمْ أَوْ هُنَّ...
- Include one nominal sentence.
- Include one present-tense verb sentence.
- Include a dual or plural form.
- Answer one audience question: مَنْ هُوَ؟ مَنْ هِيَ؟ مَنْ هُمْ؟
### Writing workshop My family or class
Write 7–10 connected sentences. Avoid repeating names by using pronouns carefully.
### Listening
Track who each pronoun refers to as speakers mention family, friends, classmates and groups.
### Reading
Use pronouns and agreement clues to follow references across a text.
### Speaking
Move naturally between أَنَا , نَحْنُ , and third-person forms when extending answers.
### Writing
Reduce repetition, connect ideas and maintain accurate subject–verb agreement.

## Repair the mistakes students make most often
### ❌ Confusing أَنْتَ and أَنْتِ
Choose by the person you are addressing, not by the speaker.
[example] يَا مَرْيَمُ، أَنْتِ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ.
### ❌ Using هُنَّ for a mixed group
هُنَّ is for an all-female human group. A mixed group normally uses هُمْ .
### ❌ Mismatching the verb
Do not write هِيَ يَدْرُسُ . Use هِيَ تَدْرُسُ .
### ❌ Translating “is” literally
For a simple present description, write هُوَ طَالِبٌ , not a word-for-word English structure.
### ❌ Treating dual as plural
Exactly two people need أَنْتُمَا / هُمَا , not أَنْتُمْ / هُمْ .
### ❌ Overusing explicit pronouns
Explicit pronouns are correct, but a verb may already contain the subject. Use the pronoun when it adds clarity, contrast or emphasis.

[callout] Stretch: non-human plurals Plural nouns for non-human things often take feminine singular agreement: الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ. هِيَ مُفِيدَةٌ. This is an important later pattern. Do not use هُنَّ merely because there are several books.
## 🎮 Who Is It? — اِخْتَرِ الضَّمِيرَ!

A scene appears: some people, and your relationship to them — are you speaking , speaking to them, or speaking about them? Run the three questions and pick the pronoun. Eight rounds. 👥 Breakout teams — the dual rounds separate the champions!
## Your complete revision summary
### Choose the pronoun
Person → number → gender. Decide in that order.
### Build a description
Pronoun + noun, adjective or place phrase. No separate present “am/is/are”.
### Agree the verb
Check the present-tense prefix and ending, especially dual and feminine plural.
### ➡️ Bridge to Lesson 2
Independent pronouns can become a map for attached possessive endings:
[example] أَنَا ← كِتَابِي I → my book
[example] هُوَ ← كِتَابُهُ he → his book

Complete aloud or in writing:
[example] أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْتَعْمِلَ الضَّمَائِرَ لِـ... I can use pronouns to...
